params.name: limit
params.description: The number of records to retrieve. If this parameter is omitted, Tenable Web App Scanning uses the default value of `10`. The minimum value is `0` and the maximum value is `200`. If you need to retrieve more than 200 records, use the offset value to iterate through page responses.

params.name: offset
params.description: The starting record to retrieve. If this parameter is omitted, Tenable Web App Scanning uses the default value of `0`.

params.name: sort
params.description:
The field you want to use to sort the results by along with the sort order. The field is specified first, followed by a colon, and the order is specified second (`asc` or `desc`). For example, `name:desc` would sort results by the `name` field in descending order.

If you specify multiple fields, the fields must be separated by commas. For example, `name:desc,created_at:asc` would first sort results by the `name` field in descending order and then by the `created_at` field in ascending order.

Returns a list of web application scan configurations. If a scan has been run using the configuration, the list also contains information about the last scan that was run.
Requires the Basic [16] user role or the `WAS.SCAN_WAS.READ` custom role privilege. Additionally, requires the Can View [16] scan permission. See [Roles](doc:roles) and [Permissions](doc:permissions).

params.name: config_id
params.description: The UUID of the scan configuration that you want to retrieve details for.

Returns details for the specified scan configuration.
Requires the Scan Operator [24] user role or the `WAS.SCAN_WAS.READ` custom role privilege. Additionally, requires the Can Execute [32] scan permission. See [Roles](doc:roles) and [Permissions](doc:permissions).

params.description: If updating an existing scan configuration, the UUID of the scan configuration you want to update. If creating a new scan configuration, a new UUID generated with a tool like `uuidgen`.

Moves the scan configuration to the specified folder.
Requires the Basic [16] user role or the `WAS.SCAN_WAS.READ` custom role privilege. See [Roles](doc:roles).

params.name: config_id
params.description: The UUID of the scan configuration you want to delete.

items.docs:
Deletes the specified scan configuration and all associated scan history and vulnerabilities. You cannot delete a scan configuration if a scan based on that configuration is currently running.
Requires the Scan Manager [40] user role or the `WAS.SCAN_WAS.MANAGE` custom role privilege. Additionally, requires the Can Edit [64] scan permission. See [Roles](doc:roles) and [Permissions](doc:permissions).

params.name: config_id
params.description:
The UUID of the scan configuration.

**Note:** The `config_id` can be retrieved from the URI provided in the `Location` header of the `202 Accepted` response from the [POST /was/v2/configs](ref:was-v2-config-create) or [PUT /was/v2/configs/{config_id}](ref:was-v2-config-upsert) request used to create or update the scan configuration.

params.name: tracking_id
params.description:
The tracking UUID for the request you want to retrieve the status for. 

**Note:** The `tracking_id` can be retrieved from the URI provided in the `Location` header of the `202 Accepted` response from the [POST /was/v2/configs](ref:was-v2-config-create) or [PUT /was/v2/configs/{config_id}](ref:was-v2-config-upsert) request used to create or update the scan configuration.

items.docs:
Tracks the current status of a scan configuration creation, update, or upsert process. When creating or updating a scan configuration, this endpoint can be used to determine the current status of the request. You can poll this endpoint using a sensible pause duration between each request until a `completed` or `failed` status is returned.

params.name: config_id
params.description: The UUID of the scan configuration to export in HOCON format for WAS CI/CD mode. You can use the [POST /was/v2/configs/search](ref:was-v2-config-search) endpoint to determine the UUID of the scan configuration you want to export.

items.docs:
Downloads the specified scan configuration in HOCON (Human-Optimized Config Object Notation) format for use with WAS Docker images in CI/CD (continuous integration / continuous delivery) mode. 

You can integrate Tenable WAS Docker images with GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, CircleCI, or Bamboo to scan builds and prevent vulnerabilities before your code and applications are deployed.
